key_insight: A hybrid front nanocone plus embedded nanohole architecture improves light trapping in thin-film silicon by reducing reflection and boosting internal scattering.
engineering_relevance: This design provides a practical path to higher-efficiency, thermally robust thin-film silicon solar cells without increasing absorber thickness.
method: Optimize nanocone and nanohole geometry with FDTD optical simulations.
Couple optical results to electrical device modeling under optimized doping.
Evaluate coupled opto-electro-thermal performance up to 45°C.
evidence_signal: The optimized cell achieves 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retention at 45°C.
watch_item: The nanocone-nanohole structure may add fabrication complexity and sensitivity to dimensional tolerances in real device manufacturing.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
